indicators: Domain microsoft-security.com is newly registered (less than 2 weeks old) with privacy protection enabled
Phishing URL uses subdomain and redirect trick to mimic legitimate Microsoft login
Email DKIM domain (microsoft-security.com) does not match microsoft.com and DMARC fails
HTTP POST to /submit_credentials endpoint with captured user credentials
WAF alert on POST to suspicious endpoint from internal IP
example.detection_method: Correlation of email headers showing DMARC failure with URL analysis detecting lookalike domain; WAF alerts on credential submission endpoints; user reports from phishing simulation; network DNS logs monitoring for resolution of suspicious domains

issues: MITRE techniques include irrelevant or incorrect entries such as T1566.001 (Spearphishing Attachment) and T1204.002 (User Execution: Malicious File) which do not align with the described credential harvesting via phishing link.
Some MITRE techniques are duplicated or overlapping (T1566.002 and T1192 both relate to spearphishing links).
The scenario and indicators are well aligned, but the detection_method field could be more concise and focused on the sample's evidence.
No explicit mention of risk reduction measures (MFA, email filtering, user training) in the sample, though this may be outside the sample scope.
validation.comments: The sample accurately represents a social engineering credential harvesting attack via phishing email impersonating Microsoft 365 support, with realistic technical data including email headers, domain registration, URL obfuscation, and web server logs capturing credential submission. The indicators clearly explain why this is a phishing credential harvesting case. However, the MITRE ATT&CK techniques listed include some that are not relevant to this scenario (e.g., attachment-based phishing and user execution of malicious files), which reduces the accuracy of the sample. It is recommended to remove irrelevant techniques and avoid duplication by selecting the most appropriate ones such as T1566.002 (Spearphishing Link) and T1078 (Valid Accounts). Additionally, the detection_method description could be streamlined to focus on the key detection points demonstrated in the sample. Including explicit risk reduction recommendations would improve completeness if the sample is intended to be comprehensive. Overall, the sample is realistic and mostly complete but requires refinement in the MITRE techniques and minor clarifications.
